notes: Good T1 Trick Shot steal of Fujii Asset Retrieval, but then clicked for credits T3-T11 up to 31 credits with nothing to spend on and no breakers until Ika T9, ignoring naked remotes (Moon Pool, Cohort Guidance, Wage Workers). Never ran Server 1 (one unrezzed ice) while Regenesis (installed T8, scored T9) and Sting! (installed T9, scored T10) sat there, and finally facechecked Anansi T12 with 5 cards, which nearly flatlined.

Coherent NBN tag/damage plan that ended in a Tsarevna flatline T16, but it put naked Regolith Mining Licenses into remotes that got trashed (T1, T8) and dropped AMAZE Amusements in the Archives root. False Lead (T9) and Tomorrow's Headline (T14) were stolen from Server 5 behind only Ping plus Tsarevna while the Corp sat on 25+ credits and never used the Runner's tags with End of the Line.

Spent all 5 credits on Carmen T1, then stayed at 0 credits for about 30 turns, running an open HQ 4 times a turn to see the same Behold!/Degree Mill/Gaslight cards (T3-T10) and absorbing endless Behold! and VSA tags against an End of the Line deck. From T27 it repeatedly ran into the known Unsmiling Tsarevna with a 2-3 card grip, trashing Buzzsaw and Cleaver, and only won because the Corp decked on T33.

Solid start: Trojan Horse trashed Echelon T2 and Send a Message was scored T6, though Above the Law was lost T1 behind a single ice to Inside Job. After that it was very slow against a Runner who only clicked for credits, sitting on 30-43 credits, advancing ice for Built to Last money, discarding 3 cards T26, and taking until T28 to score the third Send a Message.

Good aggression: Degree Mill steal from HQ T4 and a Trick Shot T9 that took Tomorrow's Headline and False Lead. Ran the naked Server 1 Degree Mill three times on T5-T6 and declined every time instead of installing two cards first to pay its cost, and the Corp scored it T7. Also re-ran R&D into unbroken Tsarevna on T9, losing Euler and Simulchip.

Clicked for credits T1-T3 and T7-T9 while discarding cards, never built a remote, and left HQ behind a single Ping, so Bellona (T3 and T9) and False Lead (T4) were stolen from HQ for the loss on T9. End of the Line T5 was a good play, but there was no scoring plan.

Facechecked HQ T1 against a net-damage clone deck and lost 3 cards to Anemone. T3 spent two clicks installing and immediately trashing Fermenter, then used the last click on an R&D run that hit Byte!, ending the turn tagged with 2 cards and no clicks to clear the tag, so End of the Line flatlined it T4.

Strong T3 Trick Shot that bankrupted the Corp, but T1-T2 were idle credit clicks and T5-T12 had many repeated same-turn R&D runs that could only re-access the same top card. Let Regenesis in Server 3 (installed T9) score T10 without a run, then T14 ran unknown ice on Server 3 with 4 cards against Personal Evolution, took Anansi damage, and was flatlined by stealing Fujii Asset Retrieval.

Never installed an agenda or built a scoring server, clicking for credits most turns up to 31 credits and discarding up to 3 cards a turn (T6, T8, T13). False Lead x2 (T10, T11), Degree Mill (T13) and Tomorrow's Headline (T16) were stolen from an HQ guarded only by Ping.

Clean Weyland game: Send a Message scored T4 behind Border Control, NGO Front and Government Subsidy money, then two SDS Drone Deployments in parallel iced remotes (Pharos) that won T15, with one SDS trashing Unity. Minor oddities were heavy ice-advancing for credits and a slow middle game.

Efficient: See How They Run scored T4 and Fujii T7 from a Diviner-protected remote, and Byte! traps in an open R&D finished a flatline T9. The only slip was installing False Lead (T4) into the same one-ice server, where it was stolen T5.

Good remote pressure T6-T9 stole Oracle Thinktank and two False Leads through Tsarevna, but face-tanking that ice drained the grip and money, leaving it at 0-3 credits and tagged against NBN for about ten turns. End of the Line hit T16 and T20, and much of that stretch was empty Archives runs and credit clicks. Breakers (Echelon, Gauss) only came out T23 for the winning HQ runs on Project Beale.

Clicked for credits almost every turn T1-T19, reaching 36 credits, with R&D unprotected until T13 (Stoke the Embers stolen T11) and a card discarded every turn, including Tomorrow's Headline, which was stolen from Archives T16. It won anyway late with three Artificial Cryptocrash and Freedom of Information from one remote against a broke Runner.

Put all money into Carmen T1, then sat at 0 credits for 27 turns making four same-turn R&D runs a turn that re-accessed the same top card. From T13 it took a VSA tag on every run and piled up dozens of tags against an End of the Line deck, losing Daily Casts and taking a 4-damage End of the Line T19. The win came only because the Corp decked on T28.

Stole Above the Law T1 and both SDS Drone Deployments (T7, T18) through a steady Aumakua + WAKE Implant R&D lock, which was a sensible plan. Economy sat at 0-3 credits all game after spending everything on Echelon/Unity T1, it ran Server 1 T4 into unrezzed Tree Line and R&D T5 into Akhet, and it wasted Dirty Laundry T11 by running into Akhet with no money to break it.

Clicked for credits T1 and T2 with no ice on HQ while holding agendas, losing Offworld Office, Artificial Cryptocrash and Stoke the Embers to free HQ runs, and installed its first ice only on T3 just before losing. T3 also wasted a click playing IP Enforcement for no effect.

Never contested the single scoring remote despite 10-14 credits: on T4 it clicked for credits while Send a Message sat advanced in Server 1 (Corp at 4 credits). T6 Pinhole Threading reached SDS Drone Deployment with no program to trash, and T7 it ran HQ instead, and T11 it installed Echelon and clicked for credits while the final Send a Message was advanced, losing T12.

Very passive T3-T8, clicking for credits to 22 and discarding every turn with only one remote, though Snare! in Server 2 and Tatu-Bola/Data Loop protected House of Knives (T10), Fujii (T12) and Hybrid Release (T15). Spent down to 1-3 credits by T13-T15, and the flatline came partly from the Runner's own Burner putting Sting! on top of R&D.

Strong tempo: See How They Run scored T3 and False Lead T7 behind a single Semak-samun the Runner kept bouncing off, with two Bladderworts and Phoneutria on R&D grinding the grip to a flatline T10. A brief stretch at 0 credits T3-T6 was the only oddity.

Won T11 by hammering an unprotected R&D (Offworld Office, Stoke the Embers x2) and an HQ facecheck for Freedom of Information, but sat at 0 credits T1-T7 after Begemot. Most clicks were repeated same-turn R&D runs that could only see the same top card, and it never checked or trashed the remote assets (Working Prototype, Public Access Plaza, Holo Man).
